response.query: bacalhau à brás traditional dish Portugal
response.answer: Bacalhau à brás is a traditional Portuguese dish made with shredded salt cod, onions, and thinly fried potato matchsticks, all bound with eggs. The dish is usually garnished with black olives and fresh cilantro or parsley. The main ingredients include salt cod, potatoes, eggs, and onion. The origin of the recipe is uncertain, but it is said to have originated in the late 19th century in Bairro Alto, Lisbon. The name "à brás" is believed to come from a 19th-century Lisbon tavern or restaurant called Braz. The dish is typically served with a side of boiled or steamed veggies or a fresh salad, crusty bread, and a dry white wine like Vinho verde.

results.title: Bacalhau à Brás Recipe: Portuguese Salt Cod with Eggs
results.content:
Bacalhau à brás is a Portuguese dish made with shredded salt cod, thin fried potato matchsticks, onions and eggs cooked until just set. It’s usually topped with black olives and fresh cilantro. You’ll find the dish on tasca menus all over Lisbon.

What does “à brás” mean?

It means “in the style of Brás.” Most food historians trace the name to a 19th-century Lisbon tavern owner or restaurant called Braz, spelled with a z in old Portuguese. Nobody knows for sure who made it first. [...] Dish: Bacalhau à brás (i.e. Brás-style salt cod)
 Cuisine: Portuguese (Lisbon)
 Main ingredients: Salt cod, potatoes, eggs, onion
 Soak time: 36 to 48 hours (change the water every 8 hours)
 Prep time: 20 minutes
 Cook time: 40 minutes
 Servings: 2 as a main or 4 as an appetizer
 Skill level: Easy once the cod is soaked
 Equipment: Cast iron skillet or air fryer, large sauté pan, chef’s knife
 Pair with: Vinho verde or another dry white wine

## The History of Bacalhau à Brás [...] What are the main ingredients in bacalhau à brás?

The three essential ingredients are salt cod, potatoes and eggs. Onion, garlic, bay leaves, cilantro, olive oil and olives complete the dish.

How long should I soak salt cod for bacalhau à brás?

Soak it for 36 to 48 hours in the refrigerator and change the water every 8 hours. At 36 hours the cod is still a little salty, so season carefully. You can soak it for longer, but you’ll lose the briny funk that makes this dish work.

results.content:
After its long soak, the fish is then cooked until it’s tender and flaky, and then shredded into small pieces. The potatoes are fried, onions cooked until they’re soft, and the eggs are beaten and added to the mixture to cook. This is the base of the dish.

Our version of the recipe also includes sundried black olives, garlic and white wine. There are many variations out there and I won’t claim that ours is the original version, but it is delicious!
